### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between the completion of A32 and the completion of A29 was about 1.0 hour on average (median about 1.03 hours, typical range roughly 0.9–1.15 hours); in the later window it was about 0.5 hours (median about 0.48 hours, typical range roughly 0.44–0.53 hours), and the spread narrowed to about half. The pair was observed as consecutive completions 44 times in each window (about 22 in 100 traces). [TWAIT001]
- The same near-halving appears for the other three predecessors of A29: from A33 the gap fell from about 0.95 to about 0.49 hours (58 gaps before, 43 after), from A34 from about 0.99 to about 0.50 hours (40 before, 62 after), and from A35 from about 0.99 to about 0.48 hours (58 before, 51 after) — each pair seen in roughly 20–30 of 100 traces per window. [TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004]
- All four gaps decreased by a similar amount, about 0.45–0.56 hours, and each difference is larger than in 1999 of 2000 random re-splits of the pooled traces. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004]
- The frequency of the consecutive pairs also shifted somewhat: A33 followed by A29 fell from 58 to 43 occurrences, while A34 followed by A29 rose from 40 to 62. [TWAIT002, TWAIT003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a timing change centred on A29: in the later window, the elapsed time from the completion of any of its predecessors A32, A33, A34 and A35 to the completion of A29 is roughly half of what it was in the earlier window (about 1 hour down to about 0.5 hours), and the gaps also became more uniform. Supporting signs: the four time items agree in direction and magnitude, each rests on 40–62 observed gaps per window, and the time family produced 4 qualifying items where only about 0.01 would be expected if nothing had changed — many times the chance expectation — while the control-flow family produced none (0 against roughly 0.3 expected), consistent with a timing change without structural rearrangement. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004]

Limitation and competing explanation: T_WAIT measures elapsed time between consecutive completions, so the evidence cannot separate a shorter wait before A29 starts from A29 itself being completed faster (or the predecessors completing earlier); the four pairs also share the same endpoint, so they describe one underlying difference rather than four independent changes. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004]

Other differences: the number of consecutive completions shifted for two pairs — A33→A29 became less frequent (58 to 43) and A34→A29 more frequent (40 to 62) — but no control-flow indicator passed the screening thresholds, so these remain unconfirmed hints of changed adjacency rather than part of the main hypothesis. [TWAIT002, TWAIT003]
